newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: AFFCO confident beef prices will turn.
newsitem.headline: AFFCO confident beef prices will turn.

text.p: AFFCO Holdings Ltd Chairman Peter Jackson told the annual meeting on Thursday the worst was over for beef prices and that they should start to turn in 1997.
The high calf kill in 1995 and 1996 seasons would have an impact on beef kills in the North Island, but the reduction was less than expected six months ago, he said.
Jackson expected to see a firming in the U.S. beef market in mid to late 1997.

"With the massive U.S. cow kill in the fourth quarter of 1996, there is general consensus that we will see a firming of the U.S. beef market in the second to third quarter of 1997," Jackson said. "I am confident that we have seen the worst and will see the market turn this coming year."
A third of AFFCO's lamb revenues now come from chilled product, equating to 16 percent in tonnage terms of AFFCO lamb.
"This gives some idea of the potential still there to increase chilled product to the world market," Jackson said.
Of AFFCO's total lamb kill, over 80 percent is further processed, leaving a small amount for the commodity carcass trade.
The company had an optimistic view of the lamb market for the current season and there was "considerable certainty" for the future.

Chief Executive Don Manson said the company was in a strong financial position, which allowed it flexibility to be able to move on an acquisition or capital expenditure initiative without over-burdening the company with debt.
AFFCO made an annual operating profit of NZ$26.5 million in the year to September, up 9.5 percent on last year's result and 19.2 percent ahead of prospectus forecasts.
Jackson, commenting on the company's share price, said that as it delivered strong results, he believed analysts and the investors would gather confidence in AFFCO.
The stock last traded at NZ$0.63 against a year high of NZ$0.71 and a low of $0.47.
